QA automation engineer with 7 years of experience, including the last two focused primarily on CI/CD pipelines, test environments and build tooling. Owns GitLab CI pipelines and merge-request ephemeral environments for three product teams. Hands-on experience with Docker, Helm, Kubernetes at namespace level, and personal k3s and GitOps projects. QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure) | Odrava Health Software, Wroclaw | 2021–Present

- Reduced average pipeline duration from 38 to 14 minutes by parallelising test jobs, caching dependencies and separating end-to-end tests into their own stage; monthly CI runner costs fell by about 30%.

- Introduced a Java and Selenium automated regression suite for the largest client project.

Customer Support Specialist (2nd line) | Brightmill Software House | 2018–2019

Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps | Personal | 2024–2025

- Reduced average pipeline duration from 38 to 14 minutes and monthly CI runner costs by about 30%.
- Technologies: GitLab CI, Docker, pytest-xdist.

CERTIFICATIONS & PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
ISTQB Foundation Level | 2019

Polish (native), English (C1), German (A2)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured and professionally written CV. It presents measurable outcomes, clear technical scope, and a credible transition from QA automation into DevOps/platform engineering. The experience bullets are concise and effective, especially the pipeline reduction, runner-cost reduction, ephemeral environments, and flaky-test improvements. The selected infrastructure projects add useful evidence beyond the candidate’s formal job titles. The main content limitation is that the CV sometimes presents DevOps-adjacent experience without clearly distinguishing production infrastructure ownership from test infrastructure and personal learning projects. The phrase “Transitioning toward” is truthful, but it also signals that the candidate is not yet operating at the full scope of the advertised contractor role.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible: standard section headings, conventional reverse-chronological structure, readable text formatting, and strong keyword coverage for GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Helm, Kubernetes, Terraform, AWS, Linux, Python, Bash, PostgreSQL, Prometheus, Grafana, and Argo CD. It should parse well and has a high AI-screening probability for QA infrastructure, CI/CD, test platform, and junior-to-mid DevOps roles. Screening probability for this specific role is moderate rather than high because the document does not contain supported evidence for Terragrunt, mTLS, network design, systems architecture, practical security, or production cloud operations. Do not add those terms merely to match the advertisement. “Cloud learning” appropriately limits the AWS claim, and the CKA preparation statement is appropriately transparent.
critique.job_alignment_feedback:
The CV aligns well with the analytical, improvement-focused, infrastructure automation, observability, Linux, and clear-documentation aspects of the role. It shows hands-on ownership of CI/CD pipelines, ephemeral environments, Helm deployments, namespace-level Kubernetes work, monitoring, Terraform in a personal project, and technical onboarding documentation. It also provides some evidence of leading technical improvements through pipeline optimization and enabling QA and product teams to review changes.

The principal alignment gaps are substantive rather than writing defects: the candidate does not show strong Terraform or any Terragrunt experience; the original information does not establish systems architecture or system-design experience; it does not show mTLS, network design, or broader practical security work; it does not show IoT, automotive, or remote-device integration; and it does not show backend/full-stack development. AWS experience is limited to learning-level EC2 and S3 basics. The candidate has Linux exposure, but no virtual-machine experience is documented. The CV is therefore a credible match for a junior-to-mid DevOps, platform, CI/CD, or test-infrastructure position, but it does not currently demonstrate the breadth expected of this cloud infrastructure contractor role.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL / HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS
1. In the Professional Summary, make the scope distinction and strongest transferable evidence more explicit. Replace “Transitioning toward a full-time DevOps or platform engineering role” with wording such as: “Moving from QA automation into DevOps/platform engineering, with hands-on ownership of CI/CD pipelines, ephemeral Kubernetes test environments, observability dashboards, and infrastructure automation.” This remains truthful while presenting the relevant experience more directly.

2. In the Technical Skills section, add the supported tool “GitLab API” under “Programming & Scripting” or “Infrastructure & CI/CD,” because the original portfolio states that it was used for the flaky-test dashboard. Also add “pytest-xdist” under “Testing & Quality,” because it is documented in the CI Pipeline Speed-up project. These are relevant ATS keywords that are currently omitted.

3. In the Professional Experience section under Odrava Health Software, add a bullet based on the original candidate information: “Wrote an internal guide explaining CI workflows and pipeline operation; the guide is now used for team onboarding.” The current CV mentions technical documentation in the summary but does not include this concrete accomplishment in the role where it occurred.

4. In the same Odrava Health section, retain the existing “mentored two QA interns” information but make its location and impact clearer. For example: “Mentored two QA interns in 2023 on test automation and CI workflows.” This provides additional evidence for communication, knowledge sharing, and bringing colleagues along.

5. In the Odrava Health bullets and the “Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments” project, clarify that the Kubernetes work was performed on a shared cluster with namespace-level access. For example, change “deployed through GitLab CI and Helm to the company’s shared Kubernetes cluster” to “deployed through GitLab CI and Helm to namespaces on the company’s shared Kubernetes cluster.” This prevents recruiters from interpreting the document as claiming cluster administration or production platform ownership.

6. In the Homelab project, distinguish the scope of the cloud work more precisely. Change “Provisioned infrastructure for a small Hetzner VPS with Terraform in a personal account” to “Provisioned a small Hetzner VPS in a personal account using Terraform.” This avoids overstating the scale of the infrastructure while preserving the useful Terraform evidence.

MINOR ATS / PRESENTATION ENHANCEMENTS
7. In the “Cloud learning” skills line, change “AWS (EC2 and S3 basics)” to “AWS: EC2 and S3 basics (learning/personal use).” This makes the experience level immediately clear to both ATS reviewers and recruiters.

8. In the Professional Summary or Technical Skills section, describe the observability work using the job’s supported term “observability,” while retaining the concrete tools. For example: “Built observability dashboards with Grafana, Prometheus, and Loki for test and homelab environments.” Only use Prometheus and Loki in relation to the homelab, where the original information supports them.

9. In the CI Pipeline Speed-up project, add “GitLab API” only if retaining the separate flaky-dashboard evidence in the CV; otherwise, keep the project focused on pipeline optimization. Avoid adding terms such as Terragrunt, mTLS, network design, production on-call, or cluster administration because the candidate information does not support them.
